text.p: - "Godfather" of the Kremlin versus "Forbes", writes the daily about Boris Berezovsky's intention to sue the magazine for libel. The Forbes article, published on December 30, 1996, implies that the top Russian official is closely connected to criminal business structures.

- Tough and urgent measures are needed to improve tax collection in Russia, the top tax police official is quoted as saying in connection with Russia's Interior Minister being given extra powers to coordinate fight against economic crime.
- The paper says a tragedy is unfolding in Tajikistan, where rebels shot dead one of about a dozen Russian and foreign hostages late on Thursday.
- Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov has been given carte blanche in his campaign against economic crime and corruption after meeting President Boris Yeltsin in the Kremlin.
- Russia's Prosecutor General Yuri Skuratov urges the state to improve its legislation backing up law enforcement agencies in their fight against crime.

- Russians will pay Western rates for municipal services despite receiving considerably lower wages. The paper links the government's tougher social policy with a new loan that will be given to Russia by the International Monetary Fund.
- Newly elected president of Chechnya Aslan Maskhadov has started to form a new government and expects his former election rivals to become his close aides.
- The present state of Russia's army is turning into a national catastrophe, says a statement of independent experts.
